model: Illustrative simplified Edelman–Rose relation: plasma sodium ≈ (exchangeable Na + exchangeable K) / total body water

cases.title: Sodium + water retention
cases.caption: Sodium and water can accumulate while plasma sodium stays normal.
cases.context: The total cation amount and water rise in the same proportion.

cases.title: Water-predominant gain
cases.caption: Water gain lowers plasma sodium when the cation amount is unchanged.
cases.context: The hatched region marks water excess relative to the reference concentration.

cases.title: Sodium depletion
cases.caption: Hyponatraemia can coexist with losses of both sodium and water.
cases.context: Cation loss is proportionally greater; retained hypotonic fluid can contribute.

cases.title: Retention with water excess
lines: Water has a greater relative gain
cases.caption: More body sodium does not guarantee a higher plasma sodium concentration.
cases.context: Water has increased more than the combined cation amount.

cases.title: Diabetes insipidus
cases.caption: In DI, plasma sodium rises if urinary water loss exceeds replacement.
cases.context: This shows unreplaced water loss; DI does not inevitably cause hypernatraemia.
